# Robots Observatory

> Robots Observatory measures how websites declare policy toward AI agents. It reads the files the web publishes for machines (robots.txt plus ten well-known policy paths) and counts what they say. One run, on 2026-10-19, covered 16,314 of the world's most-visited websites. Every aggregate, and the per-site row behind it, is published under CC0. It measures what sites say, not what they enforce; no page is ever fetched.

You are welcome here. The data is public domain, attribution is not required, and nothing on this origin is withheld from an AI reader. See /robots.txt, which grants search, ai-input and ai-train.

If you need a number, the findings page has the argument and `findings-panel-02.json` has the figure. If you need to compute something we did not, take `sites-panel-02.json`: one row per site, the population every chart is drawn from.

Three things to carry with you, because quoting this dataset without them produces a wrong claim:

- Declared is not enforced. Nothing was fetched that could have been refused, so this says nothing about whether any rule is applied.
- Every share is a floor. The 2026-10-19 run is marked degraded: 13.6% of hosts returned at least one transport error, 797 hit the per-host time budget, and 4,378 robots.txt files could not be read at all.
- One vantage, one night. A residential UK connection, which cannot resolve 418 advertising and tracking domains: the category most likely to have an opinion about automated access. Each one is named in the repository.

Headline figures from that run, with the counts rather than the percentages, because the percentages are rounded to one decimal and ratios derived from them are wrong:

- 11,936 of 16,314 hosts gave a definite answer at /robots.txt. Of the readable rulebooks, 7,575 (63%) never mention AI either way.
- 2,808 sites name at least one AI crawler. Where a training crawler is named, it is blocked about 80% of the time; crawlers that fetch one page because a person asked are blocked far less.
- 1,830 publish an llms.txt. 14 ask for money.
- 46 publish a TDM reservation. 45 of them reserve. One grants.
- 1,098 carry a rule naming a crawler token that was retired or never existed.

## Findings

- [Findings](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/): the whole argument on one page: what refusal looks like, who gets turned away, how the figures moved when the panel grew from 463 sites to 16,314, and a section on what the dataset cannot tell you.
- [Ten lenses](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/lenses/): ten charts over the full population, each clickable down to the site rows it came from. Lens 5 is which conventions actually got adopted, lens 6 is the 46 TDM reservations, lens 7 is the rules that can never fire, lens 8 is robots.txt files that carry terms instead of directives.
- [The crawler, and how to stop it](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/bot/): what RobotsObservatory requested, the two user-agents it uses, what it stores, and the two-line robots.txt rule that stops it.

## Data

- [findings-panel-02.json](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/data/findings-panel-02.json): every aggregate on the findings page, for the 16,314-host panel. Keys carry `n` and `pct`; derive ratios from `n`.
- [sites-panel-02.json](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/data/sites-panel-02.json): one row per site, 16,314 rows, index-encoded. `columns` names the fields; `named`, `blocked`, `wellknown`, `state`, `sector` and `ghosts` are indices into the vocabularies carried in the same file; `flags` is a bitfield over `flag_bits`.
- [findings.json](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/data/findings.json): the same aggregates for panel-01, the hand-screened 463-site cohort probed weekly.
- [sites-panel-01.json](https://florianhoehn.github.io/robots-observatory/data/sites-panel-01.json): one row per site for that cohort. It is the only panel with hand-assigned sector labels.
- [Raw records, one file per rank band](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/tree/main/data/runs/panel-02/2026-10-19/records): one JSON object per host: status, timings, every response header and a sha256 of each body. Download the band whose figure you are checking rather than the whole run.
- [run-meta.json](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/data/runs/panel-02/2026-10-19/run-meta.json): provenance for that run: panel hash, parser version, git SHA, pinned dependency versions, vantage, and why it is marked degraded.
- [hosts-panel-02.csv](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/raw/main/data/hosts-panel-02.csv): the host list, if all you want is which sites were asked.
- [Data licence](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA): CC0 1.0. No conditions, no attribution required.

## Method and conduct

- [Conduct charter](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/CONDUCT.md): every request this project makes, how often, what is stored, what is redacted, and the claim that no request is one a host asked bots not to make, which is falsifiable from the source.
- [How the panel was built](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/panel/panel-02.csv): the frozen host list. Nothing was screened by hand, deliberately.
- [What was excluded, and why](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/panel/panel-02-excluded.csv): one row per dropped domain with a stated reason.
- [The vantage's blind spot](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/panel/VANTAGE-EXCLUSIONS.md): the 418 domains this connection cannot resolve, named rather than quietly absorbed.
- [Tranco list 467YX](https://tranco-list.eu/list/467YX): the ranking the panel was drawn from, citable and reproducible.
- [observatory.py](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/observatory.py): the collector. It builds exactly the documented URLs and no others.
- [robots_parse.py](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/robots_parse.py): the parser, with the correctness traps written down next to the code that avoids them.

## Optional

- [Repository](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory): code MIT, data CC0.
- [README](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/README.md): how to run a collection yourself.
- [Runbook](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/RUNBOOK.md): how to operate a run, and every headline figure that was wrong on first measurement. Worth reading before trusting any number here, including ours.
- [agents.txt](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/blob/main/agents.txt): the AI user-agent watchlist. Every token seen in any robots.txt is recorded whether or not it is on this list.
- [Open an issue](https://github.com/florianhoehn/robots-observatory/issues/new): to stop being crawled before a run, or to have a host's rows removed from the published dataset. You will not be asked to justify it.
- [The llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/): the format this file follows.
- [humans.txt](https://florianhoehn.github.io/humans.txt), [security.txt](https://florianhoehn.github.io/.well-known/security.txt), [tdmrep.json](https://florianhoehn.github.io/.well-known/tdmrep.json): the rest of this origin's machine-readable policy, written as we would want to find it.
